In short

Monday Marketing Company (MMC) is an India-based marketing agency for D2C, B2B and education brands. Its services sit in five systems: paid media, search and conversion, brand, technology, and content.

  • Five systemsPaid media, search and conversion, brand, technology, and content.
  • One team runs all fiveSo the work in one system is judged by what it does for the others.
System I

Revenue Accelerators

Performance media that compounds, not just spends.

  • Performance marketingMeta, Google, Amazon and quick-commerce media run as one account, judged on contribution margin.Read the performance marketing page
  • Lead generationPaid enquiries for B2B, education and service businesses, connected to a CRM and Meta's Conversions API (CAPI) so campaigns learn from qualified leads, not form fills.Read the lead generation page
  • Retention marketingFunnels across email, WhatsApp and loyalty that nurture enquiries into customers and bring buyers back.Read the retention marketing page

Common questions

What people ask first.

What marketing services does MMC offer?

Services in five systems: Revenue Accelerators (performance marketing, lead generation, retention), Organic Growth Engines (SEO and conversion), Brand Foundation Builders (identity, UX, packaging), Technology Drivers (Shopify, websites, apps) and Content Magnets (UGC, video, social, influencers).

Do I have to buy all five systems?

No. You can start with one. The audit call shows where your biggest leak is, and we begin there.

Which service should I start with?

If ad spend is your biggest cost, start with performance marketing. If traffic is fine but few visitors buy, start with conversion. If nobody finds you in search, start with SEO. The audit call settles it.

What does it cost?

It depends on scope and, for media, on ad spend, so we quote after the audit call.

Which kinds of brands do you work with?

D2C brands, B2B companies and educational institutes, plus consumer-facing businesses such as real estate, hospitality and mobility. D2C brands buy on orders and repeat purchases. B2B and education brands buy on qualified leads and enrolments. The work is set up differently for each: see the D2C, B2B and education pages.

Not sure where to start?

Tell us the problem. We will say which system fixes it.

On a call, with a senior strategist. We look at your accounts and tell you where to start.
